name: Table Salt

sources.name: King Arthur Baking — Ingredient Weight Chart
USDA FoodData Central — Salt, table (FDC ID 173468)

notes: Fine sea salt has a crystal size and volume-to-weight ratio close enough to table salt to use this figure — an approximate substitution. Coarse sea salt is lighter by volume and shouldn't be substituted 1:1.

name: Kosher Salt (Diamond Crystal)

sources.name: King Arthur Baking — Ingredient Weight Chart

notes: Diamond Crystal flakes are hollow and much lighter by volume than table salt or Morton kosher salt — do not substitute 1:1 by volume. A bare "kosher salt" with no brand named is an assumed, approximate match to this entry (Diamond Crystal), matching how most modern US recipe developers (NYT Cooking, Bon Appétit, Serious Eats) write recipes; Morton's is roughly 2x heavier by volume, so a recipe naming Morton's specifically still matches that brand's own entry, and getting the brand wrong on a salt-heavy bake matters.
